messages:
jordan lee: FYI Riverbank wants a short POC to validate compatibility with their legacy API before we go to contracts. Main asks: prompt/response parity, stop-token behavior, and a clear cost delta if tokens increase. They also attached an infosec questionnaire.

sophia (se): Got it. I ran an initial probe against 500 representative prompts. Observations: our tokenizer merges some emoji sequences they split, leading to ~6% fewer tokens on our side for that set. Conversely, some multi-space HTML blobs they send become more tokens for us (+12%). Overall variance unpredictable by payload type.

mira patel: For the POC they'll need a reproducible harness and a compatibility shim suggestion. Can we produce a short runbook and a tiny adapter example that normalizes their inputs? Also they asked if we can disable client IP logging for the POC.

sophia (se): Adapter idea: pre-normalize to NFC, collapse multiple spaces to single spaces, remove zero-width chars, and canonicalize common emoji sequences. Also add a stop-sequence sanitizer that ensures stop tokens are token-aligned and do post-decode truncation to be safe. Quick example to hand them: ```python
# normalize text before sending to API
import unicodedata
import re

def normalize(s):
    s = unicodedata.normalize('NFC', s)
    s = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s)
    s = s.replace('\u200d','')  # remove zero-width joiner for tests
    return s
```
This reduces token deltas for our sample by ~4-7%.

tim (prod): Pricing piece: Customer expects three cost scenarios: baseline, median delta, worst-case delta. Use their stated volume 500k chats/month, avg 450 tokens/chat. Show hosted unit price vs Dedicated commit estimate. Also show streaming vs final-charge explanation (we invoice based on consumed tokens after request completes).

jordan lee: On security, can we confirm hosted can redact headers and disable XFF for their org id during the POC? They want a note for the questionnaire: "no raw client IPs are forwarded or stored in request logs for this POC" if possible.

ops-bot: Deployment job redwood-canary-1 started by @ops at 2025-11-05T09:01Z

sophia (se): Yes, for hosted POC we can turn off X-Forwarded-For and apply header redaction. We can also run the POC in a dedicated tenant with short retention (7 days) and KMS-wrapped logs. Legal needs to sign the reduced-retention addendum.

mira patel: Action items: (1) @sophia produce a token-delta CSV + 20 sample prompt pairs (ours vs theirs) by EOD Thu. (2) @tim draft cost scenarios slide and a short paragraph on billing model. (3) @jordan prep the infosec response stub and request the signed retention addendum. Schedule 30m sync with Riverbank next Tue.

sophia (se): I'll also include a small A/B test harness (shell + python) so they can run locally against both endpoints and get a simple "tokens, length, stop-aligned" report. Example harness snippet: ```bash
#!/bin/bash
# compare tokenizer counts
python compare_tokens.py --left redwood-endpoint --right legacy-endpoint --prompts sample_top100.txt
```

compare_tokens.py will produce a CSV with columns: prompt_id,left_tokens,right_tokens,delta,stop_truncation_diff

jordan lee: Great. I'll send calendar invite and attach their questionnaire. If we get legal sign-off on retention we'll enable KMS logs for the test tenant. :wave:
